title: Protocol for Inoculating Bottled Mineral Water with Bacteria for Contamination Studies
author: Ziegler, Platzer, et al.
materials:
Timing: 10–15 min
4.For this protocol, take a cylindrical funnel with a volume of 100 mL and filtrate an amount by 10 mL–100 mL of the artificial contaminated water samples.2,35.To verify Enterobacteriaceae filtrate the 100 mL of the artificial contaminated water and put the filter on Endo agar plates.
Note: For the filtration of the water samples through a porous membrane, filtration equipment is necessary.

steps.title: Prepare contaminant solution
steps.instruction: Create the bacterial inoculum and determine its initial concentration.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave a sterile glass bottle containing 1000 mL distilled water at 121 °C for 20 min for each bacterial strain.
Dilute one ceramic bead (containing ~10⁶ CFU/mL) in the autoclaved 1000 mL distilled water.
Gently invert the bottle to mix the bead suspension.
Allow the suspension to stand for 10 min; the contaminant solution is then ready.
Determine the CFU/mL of this starting solution by preparing a serial dilution, plating on tryptic soy agar, incubating, counting colonies and recording the CFU/mL.

steps.title: Set incubator temperatures
steps.instruction: Configure incubators for water storage and plate counting.

substeps.instruction: Set an incubator to 25 °C for the 31‑day incubation of the artificial contaminated water samples.
Set a second incubator to 37 °C for optimal growth when counting CFU/mL on agar plates.

steps.title: Assemble filtration apparatus
steps.instruction: Prepare the filtration set‑up and ensure proper membrane and plate conditions.

substeps.instruction: Take a cylindrical funnel with a 100 mL volume capacity.
Fit a 0.45 µm cellulose‑ester membrane disc onto the funnel; verify no leaks.
The apparatus will be used to filter 10–100 mL of each artificial contaminated water sample.
If agar plates have been stored at 4 °C, pre‑heat them to 25 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare ion chromatography eluent and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions required for anion chromatography and photometric assays.

substeps.instruction: Anion eluent stock: dissolve 42.4 g Na₂CO₃ and 4.2 g NaHCO₃ in 500 mL deionised water (final concentrations 800 mM Na₂CO₃, 100 mM NaHCO₃).
Fresh eluent for runs: dilute 20 mL of the stock solution into 1980 mL deionised water.
Reagent 1 (for ammonium): dissolve 260 g C₇H₅NaO₃ and 260 g Na₃C₆H₅O₇ in 1600 mL deionised water, then add 1.94 g sodium nitroprusside and mix.
Reagent 2 (for ammonium): dissolve 64 g NaOH in 1000 mL deionised water, then add 4 g sodium dichloride isocyanurate and mix until fully dissolved.
Nitrite‑Griess reagent: add 100 mL orthophosphoric acid to 500 mL deionised water, then add 40 g sulfanilamide, mix, and finally add 2 g naphthylethylenediamine dihydrochloride.

steps.title: Conduct chemical property analyses
steps.instruction: Measure pH, conductivity, TOC, metal ions, anions, ammonium and nitrite in the water samples.

substeps.instruction: pH: place 100 mL of the sample in a 150 mL beaker and measure pH at room temperature using the Metrohm Tritator system.
Conductivity: use the same 100 mL volume and measure with the conductometer attached to the same sample changer.
Total organic carbon (TOC): add 50 µL 2 M H₂SO₄ containing 80 g L⁻¹ sodium peroxydisulfate to a reaction tube, insert the sample, and run the TOC analyzer.
Ensure argon gas flow is set between 130 and 150 mL min⁻¹ during TOC analysis.
Dissolved metal ions: filter 100 mL of sample through a 0.45 µm membrane, add 1 mL concentrated HNO₃, and analyse Fe, Mn, Ca, Mg, Na and K by ICP‑OES (ASX‑280 sample changer, Qtegra v2.8.2944.202).

Ion chromatography (anions): dilute mineral water 1:10, load the vial into the Dionex ICS‑1100 sample changer, run the appropriate program, and before each run rinse the system with the prepared eluent to obtain a linear baseline.
Calculate water hardness from the measured Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ concentrations.
Ammonium spectrophotometry: in a reaction tube add 5 mL sample, then 0.4 mL Reagent 1 and 0.4 mL freshly prepared Reagent 2; mix, verify pH ≈12.6, and measure absorbance at 665 nm.
Nitrite spectrophotometry (Griess test): add one drop of the Griess reagent to 5 mL sample, wait 20 min, set wavelength to 540 nm and record absorbance.

steps.title: Inoculate water bottles
steps.instruction: Introduce the bacterial contaminant into the mineral water bottles.

substeps.instruction: For each experimental condition and each pathogen, prepare three sterile bottles.
Open a fresh bottle, add 1 mL of the contaminant solution prepared in Step 1, immediately reseal the bottle.
Mix the inoculated water gently by orbital shaking of the bottle.

steps.title: Incubate contaminated bottles
steps.instruction: Store the inoculated bottles for the desired exposure period.

substeps.instruction: Place the bottles in a dark area at room temperature.
Incubate for any chosen duration between 1 day and 31 days (the protocol uses 1 d, 2 d, 7 d, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, and 31 days).
Handle all bottles with biosafety precautions because of pathogenic strains.

steps.title: Filter samples and plate on Endo agar
steps.instruction: Recover bacteria from water at each time point by filtration and plating.

substeps.instruction: At each scheduled time point, open the corresponding bottle.
Place a fresh 0.45 µm filter onto the prepared cylindrical funnel; confirm no leakage.
Filter 100 mL of the inoculated water through the filter using vacuum.
Transfer the filter directly onto an Endo agar plate.

steps.title: Incubate plates and count CFU
steps.instruction: Grow colonies and determine bacterial concentration in the water samples.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the Endo agar plates for 24 h at 37 °C.
After incubation, count all colonies on each plate.
Calculate CFU mL⁻¹ for the corresponding time point using the counted colonies and the filtered volume.
Optional: for later time points, repeat filtration with 10 mL of sample (1:10 dilution) to avoid over‑crowding of colonies.

steps.title: Validate isolates on TSA
steps.instruction: Confirm the identity of recovered colonies and obtain pure cultures.

substeps.instruction: Select distinct single colonies from the Endo plates.
Streak each selected colony onto TSA agar to obtain pure cultures.
Examine colony morphology to preliminarily confirm strain identity.
Perform an oxidase test with an inoculation loop on each isolate.
Place the confirmed isolates into wells of an MS‑chip for MALDI‑TOF analysis if desired.

description: The protocol below describes a method of inoculating drinking water samples with a variety of pathogens or facultative pathogen bacteria. We describe steps for preparing bacterial solutions, inoculating mineral water bottles and other drinking water samples, filtration and incubation of the agar plates, and counting CFU/mL. We also detail procedures for determining selected chemical properties, such as anions and cations, which can also affect the bacterial growth. Timing: 1–1.5 h The purpose of this step is to confirm the respected colonies of the artificial contaminated water samples.3,1112.Select different single colonies on the plate for the identification and transfer them on TSA agar to get pure cultures.a.First, confirm your respected strains checking the morphological pattern.b.Take an inoculation loop to test whether your single colony is oxidase positive or negative.c.Pick the same colonies from pure cultures and place them on the well of the MS-chip.Note: For the determination of the respected strains, MALDI TOF analyses can be performed.
